records.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
records.summary_text:
A small US territory: federal document and airport policy applies, and the 2025–26 federal turn is felt through it (marker disputes, screening friction) with no local statute to soften it. Locally the record is quietly protective rather than hostile: the Attorney General ruled in 2017 that the human-rights law's sex provision covers transgender students — an official extension of territorial protection — and local media framed the community's position after the 2016 federal shock as 'losses... but reason for hope.'

records.name: Niue
records.summary_text:
One of the world's smallest self-governing states, in free association with New Zealand, Niue carries neither criminalisation nor protection on LGBT matters. Colonial-era offences were removed with the age of consent reported equalised by 2011, and no audited source documents enforcement against queer people at all; equally there is no recognition of same-sex relationships and no non-discrimination statute — and the principal 1966 act still shows uneven ages of majority by sex (21 men/19 women) on its face into the 2010s.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Niue
sources.claim_summary: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people in Niue face legal challenges not experienced by non-LGBTQ residents. Same-sex couples and households headed by same-sex couples are not eligible for the same legal protections available to opposite-sex married couples.
